report: Powerful TWP with a lively arm but brutal feel to command it, might be viewed more favorably as a bat had he a true defensive home. Massive frame, still some baby fat to clean up. Struggles to replicate violent arm path, leading to more free passes than Ks this summer & likely some blow-out risk. FB is up to 100 w deadzone shape: AA spin & BL-flawless efficiency, just throws it hard from a mundane slot (flashes of big mvmnt are due to the aforementioned release inconsistencies). Mixes-in low-spin SW that lacks deception & work-in-progress CH. Offensively, he just about matched Seward's spring performance in the same elite league, 18% K & 1.246 OPS. There's surely swing-and-miss to his game, but w advanced feel for the zone & enough power (T103 w wood). Plays 1B when not pitching, 20-grade speed makes a transition to OF unrealistic.

Older switch-hitting SS with the defensive polish to stick there, low offensive ceiling. Performance as righty/lefty is closely mirrored, although the lefty swing visual is clearly better (more fluid, rotates more powerfully, path is cleaner/more uphill). Well-BA power overall, yet to see him surpass 100EV in-game, but room to add muscle. Advanced feel for the zone (36% BBs this spring); a bit passive, but seems like legit pitch recognition, will benefit from a change in intent. Contact-ability isn't awe-inspiring, but shortens-up with 2 strikes & effectively avoids Ks (13%/16% this spring/summer). AA runner who steals bags freely & efficiently. Smooth hands @ SS with advanced footwork & AVG arm strength, gets rushed at times, & consistency will need to improve, particularly in regard to throwing accuracy, but expect it to with reps.

Hawaiian OF with defensive polish & a projectable frame, but underwhelming tools overall. Made a name for himself as a Sophomore on the summer circuit, but didn't do much in 2026 to raise his stock. EVs are up to 104 in BP, 99 in-game with wood. Patient hitter, seems more like a product of passivity than selectivity. Path can get steep at times, & struggles to adjust to offspeed: often ends up on his front foot, with 55% whiff on breaking pitches this summer. Reads/routes are relatively advanced in OF, but the borderline-20 run tool leaves no chance of him sticking in CF. Fringy arm strength, throws accurately with natural fade. Hoping for RF outcome if arm strength comes with physical growth, but LF's more realistic. With that in mind, I don't think the bat's in a place to warrant many trips to Hawaii this spring.

SoCal UTL with a projection body & modest present tools. Produced for AVG this spring against premier competition, albeit with too many strikeouts (21%) & minimal power production. Difficult to assess raw power, as he's a defensive hitter who struggles to get his A-swing off (particularly vs breaking balls), but in-game EVs have been well-BA to say the least. Stride direction tweaks could help him cover the outer 3rd. Has spent time in INF & OF, but with an AVG run tool & a solidly BA arm, a lot of present polish is required, something he doesn't have. Actions on the dirt are good enough where there's a chance to stick (but it would likely be @ 2B), routes in the OF are still crude. There is power to come as he strengthens the frame & with a change in intent, but that's only one of many improvements needed for Mason to be a pro prospect.

Huge SoCal C w swing-and-miss woes, betting on the impressive raw tools. More HRs than Ks this spring (13/11 in 76 PA), & up to 106 w wood, but swing decisions need a ton of work: chases high heat & low spin, without the zone-aggression or bat-to-ball to compensate. Slightly open stride makes it hard to cover outer 3rd, would be an EZ fix, has shown adjustability: began summer with upright stance & a load that drifted past his back leg, has since tidied up the operation. Arm's up to 84 behind the dish, but slow transfers push poptimes closer to fringe. Uses paddle method when blocking to moderate success, BA receiving. Based on the body & lack of present polish, I think catching is a long-shot outcome, but the arm would suit him well in a COF spot; not many reliable run times, but looks like fringe/BA speed. Star WR/TE on football team.

PD-project LHP with BA control, but possessing an intriguing pitch mix that doesn't require much projection. Med-sized frame, gets down the mound well, but arm action will need a ton of work: inverted W & big stab. Hop FB, which already grades-out as AA+ despite only sitting 92, has the spin traits to survive the switch to MLB balls. Short SL with AA spin is a legitimate weapon when thrown competitively, but limited present feel. Can't imagine the CB developing into anything more than a show-me, but has proven effective vs HSers; to my knowledge, didn't concede a hit on either breaker this summer. Could be special once a CH is added, depending on how fixable PD thinks the mechanical flaws are.

Powerful, ultra-young TWP with the summer results & raw EVs to garner interest as a bat, but whose greatest value presently is on the mound. The arsenal is somewhat weak relative to the pure arm talent, but can (maybe wishfully) be interpreted as a product of low training age. FB is up to 100, with high-variance spin efficiency (ranging from well-BA to elite); the result is a deadzone shape on avg, with flashes of big ride & run. Nothing in the deliv/release tells me these blue shapes can't be attained consistently with pro instruction. SL grades as his best pitch due to its velo, but, like the FB, seems unrefined in its intent. Fringe spin, but can still see it split into 2 legit weapons. VulcanCH is still a project. Fringe ext, advanced hip-shoulder separation, & freaky-fast arm. It's a projection play but huge upside if things click.

Young, smaller RHP with crossfire deliv & ++ extension, which, combined with 18in IVB, creates a moderately flat plane on 92mph FB. That being said, the pitch isn't deceptive above the zone & hitters have feasted on it. Struggles to replicate the shape of slurvy, low-80s breaker, leading to lmtd feel. The pitch hasn't generated whiffs or chases effectively, but hitters haven't produced against it either; given the BA shape, we'll call the latter a product of small sample size, and expect the results to regress. Mixes-in CH with uninteresting shape, located consistently armside (unclear whether this is a product of legitimate command or directional issues). Only 3 IP this spring, unsure whether it's due to injury, & too many walks this summer. Velo is up 2 ticks from 2025, should continue to rise as he adds mass onto slender frame. Late G3

Not your prototypical catcher's body: lanky 6'4 frame with room for muscle, and runs better than position+build would suggest (lmtd competitive H2F times in Synergy, but up to 28.4 ft/s on Hawkeye). AA arm strength behind the dish with inconsistent accuracy. Long legs limit his mobility, prefers to pick the ball over blocking & doesn't excel at it. Adept receiver on gloveside pitches, has a tougher time handling stuff across his body. Some defensive versatility, spent innings in INF & OF, haven't seen enough to assess either confidently. Offensively, he swings with a direct path to the ball, but underutilizes his legs, resulting with well-BA batspeed & EVs. BA production this summer, but ran a 6% K-rate, 1.244 OPS this spring vs AVG comp. Worth a follow given rare coordination for size & spring performance, but a lot left to be desired.

Stocky INF whose calling card is clearly bat-to-ball. 6% K-rate, 92% contact vs AA competition this spring en route to a 1.245 OPS. Despite the muscular build & effortful swing, he's only been up to 103 with wood, without the room-for-growth needed to project major power gains. Generally a passive hitter, but chases too much relative to his Z-swing rates. Didn't do too much to raise or lower his stock offensively this summer, but got to show-off the hands @ SS after waiting for Taj Marchand to graduate. A fringy runner, Ostergard doesn't possess the fluidity/natural twitch for SS longterm, but the hands are reliable enough to keep him on the dirt.

Sushi brings a well-rounded OF tool package to the table, highlighted by raw power output/batspeed (posted impressive EVs with wood all summer, culminating in 423ft bomb @ Camden). Sub-80 Z-Contact% across both the summer circuit & this spring @ IMG, but a couple feasible mechanical tweaks could improve the hit-tool & turn him into a 5-tool player: swings with a slightly open stride that inhibits his ability to cover the outer third (contact on inside pitches is AA), & an aggressive forward move that can make it difficult to be on-time. Sushi played RF this spring, with some hiccups early in the transitioned to CF this summer, but showed adjustability, reads looked notably better late in summer. AA runner with at least AVG raw arm strength (up to 94 on mound), there's a clear path to CF, with both corner spots available as fall-backs.

Young, twitchy OF with performance track record across spring & summer seasons. Generally a passive hitter who happily draws his walks, neither the contact rates nor peak EVs are awe-inspiring, but when he makes contact it's consistently on the barrel with a swing that's optimized to elevate. Swings out of a closed stance with a bit of an arm bar, but rotates explosively with ample batspeed. Solidly + runner with an effortless gait, stole 37 bags without being caught this spring. Defense is still a bit raw, had a tough time reading the ball off the bat @ ACG, & struggled to keep his throws on-target, but the tools suggest a CF outcome if things click with proper training. It's a fun low-floor/high-ceiling bet. Late G2.

Physical RHP who has cemented himself in my eyes as the top HS arm of the class. Can't project future improvement (other than separating the SL into multiple shapes), but it's elite stuff now w feel to command it & unmatched performance to prove. Huge ride+run FB grades out as at least plus presently; tumble+fade kickCH visually presents as his best weapon & is located comfortably armside+down, good for 64%whiff & 49%chase this summer; SL is his weakest shape, but rips through it & locates for chases, 77% whiff. Nothing but video game numbers at every level: 0.1 ERA, 0.57 K%-BB% this spring, going the distance in most starts, then nearly matched that dominance at each stop of the summer circuit. Delivery is a bit herky-jerky getting to 3/4 slot/AA extension, but adds deception & doesn't seem to negatively affect output. Not far from G0.

LHH OF with solidly BA raw power, magnified by downward attack angle & lmtd physical projection left, but AA+ grades across the rest of the board. Solidly plus runner, flashing ++ at times, arm is an impact tool as well, up to 92 on the bump & reportedly 96 from OF in 2025. Reads/routes are a bit unrefined, but goes after the ball aggressively, expect the rest to come with reps. Offensively, the carrying trait is clearly B2B, ran a 5% K-rate & 94% contact this spring en route to .527 BA. Some of those hits are beaten-out GBs, which will turn into outs as competition improves, but the contact skills persisted across the summer circuit, as did swing decisions (identifies spin quite well). Type of player that could end up a model darling 3 years down the line. Until then, hoping for power production to take a step forward.

Young northeast reliever with outlier stuff but damning command risk. Mammoth frame, controls it better than the BA extension would suggest; 3-sport athlete (4 including Ballet). Unicorn FT is up to 99 (102 in bullpen) w nearly 20in of run & plenty of sink (flashing negative IVB), but achieves the shape via an artificial-manufactured sidearm slot: whereas effective side-winders employ heavy trunk tilt during stride to help get the arm on-plane, Kuhn stays upright, forcing the arm/shoulder to set the path in isolation. Not the only mechanical flaw, but contributes to the BBs plaguing his career, & more critically, adds immense blow-out risk. Shutdown this spring, unclear if due to injury. Mixes in short, lifty SL & big, high-spin SW. Would love to scrap the chassis & rebuild around the engine, but would require a far-too-risky investment.

Older LHH INF lacking any standout tool. Gap-to-gap LDs throughout BP but in-game EVs are modest, with discouraging Z-contact across the summer circuit. Doesn't seem to pick up spin well. Easy swing works nicely uphill through the zone, but can get long at times, & accordingly gets beaten by velo. Defensively, Addison lacks the range or arm needed to stick @ SS longterm, with multiple errors @ ACG pushing down confidence in the hands. Will play his senior season @ Baylor School after beginning HS career @ Evangelical Christian. Will need to see some physical development before spring to have any real interest.

Prototypical projection arm: thin 6'4 frame, long levers, & still yet to turn 17, with velo trending up over the last calendar year. That being said, the present stuff isn't awe-inspriring. Ride-FB is largely limited by spin efficiency, CB with AA spin gets chases when thrown below the zone, might end up his best weapon if velo's to come, but struggles to replicate the shape leading to well-BA command. Mixes in CH with limited feel to lefties, grades-out as his best pitch with AA vertical separation, would love to see him throw it slower. Has faced premium competition across the summer circuit and held his own, but too many walks with BA present mix makes it hard to be head-over-heels.

Lambert is an intriguing Maryland OF without any stand-out trait to hang your hat on. Underwhelming performance this spring: 19% K, 77%contact, 1.093 OPS against competition he really should've feasted on. Swing-and-miss became a more damning issue this summer, but the bat works nicely uphill & EVs are playable: up to 103 in-game with wood. Grading the run-tool is tricky: posted BA times all summer, but roamed the OF like an AA+ runner @ UA AA game, more in-line with the 6.69 60yd he recorded there. It's possible he's been nursing a leg injury, caught him limping @ ACG. Arm is solidly AVG, as are reads/routes; he'll have a chance to stick in CF, with both corner spots open as more-realistic fall-back options. Has played enough viable INF to dream on a super-UTL role down the road.

Stiff, hulking RHP from the DR, now playing northeast prep ball. Was used sparsely out of the bullpen this spring, appears to be performance related, not due to injury. Walked the house at every stop of the summer circuit, struggling to replicate OTT slot (drops lower on SL). Lively arm, up to 97 with serious cut. Command is the limiting factor presently: zero feel for either FB or SL, with no clear path for improvement. The arm is fun, but pending an unrealistic step forward in strike-throwing this spring, Acevedo will need to prove himself @ UVA.

Posted an impressive spring vs NorCal comp: 1.260 OPS, 10.6% K-rate, 6 bombs. Lived above 100EV in BP @ ACG, then multiple basehits over 100EV in-game (against some of the better arms there). The swing works, clean uphill path, plenty of batspeed (81.6 max @ PBR ProCase), & has demonstrated adjustability w med-sized leg kick to be on-time. Already a strong kid, but it's a lean, high-waisted, wide-shouldered frame, could end up being massive. Getting some reps @ 1B, but the raw tools say he belongs in OF; routes/instincts are a bit raw presently, but arm is at least AVG (up to 88 on mound), as is run tool (didn't get a competitive H2F time @ ACG, but showcase sprint times suggest AVG with AA acceleration). Well-rounded profile, possible UTL role down the road, really intrigued.

Lean, long-limbed frame, athletic mover, & effortless delivery; it's hard to imagine more of a slamdunk velo projection. Overmatched PA competition this spring, posting an absurd 0.44% K%-BB%, then didn't waver across the summer circuit. Slight cross-fire stride will allow him to dominate lefties @ next level, AA extension & high3/4 slot aid in creating huge ride on FF (45% whiff this summer). Throws gyroSL gloveside regardless of R/L, lands it consistently. Really wish he'd throw it harder, would look to tighten the gyro spin & separate into two distinct shapes. Mix is rounded out by the occ CH, which has flashed the shape of a legit weapon when thrown. Wouldn't be surprised if he adds multiple ticks of velo by spring & starts to get 2nd-round-buzz.

Lmtd event trackrecord to judge the bat, but @ ACG he almost never chased or whiffed, albeit without the baseball-card numbers to show. Same story this spring: 6% K-rate in the competitive Tri-River League with minimal power production. Despite the contact-over-slug profile, he's been up to 100EV with wood with some room to add strength onto wide-shouldered frame & age on his side. Provides value on dirt, but doesn't have the hands or range (35 runner without the lateral mobility to compensate) to stick at SS long term. Borderline G3/G4.

Contact-first OF with lmtd present power but room to fill-out slimmer frame & age on his side. Strong spring performance vs NorCal comp highlighted by 6.5% K-rate & 92.3% contact, but has struggled this summer with wood, including a number of non-competitive swings @ ACG. Swing mechanics will take a lot of work, specifically the unloading phase; upper & lower halves rotate together, breaks posture on every swing, & handsy path works steeply downward through zone. Can't confidently say the issues are fixable. Defensively, saw him in RF but has to tools to keep a CF-outcome possible: AA footspeed, covers ground efficiently, & arm is at least AVG (up to 89 on mound). Borderline G4/5. Uncommitted currently.

Not the most athletic mover: stiff lower half/hips & BA extension, but lanky, long-limbed frame & whippy arm balance out the velo projection. Strong spring performance vs northeast comp: 61 Ks, 15 BBs in 35 IP, then continued to punch across this summer circuit (including all 5 outs @ ACG coming via K). Throws with deceptive low3/4 arm path, generating tons of run on FB, & occ killing enough IVB to create steep plane from 5.7 release height. Best offering is frisbee SW that generated 61% whiff this summer in lmtd Synergy sample, with more than enough spin to build complimentary shapes around it. Occasionally mixes in CH w minimal separation off FB. Solidly G3.

Large, strong, & athletic SoCal CF. Impressive spring performance against one of the more competitive schedules in the country, highlighted by 13% K-rate. On-paper it's a bona fide contact-first profile, but the underlying traits paint a different picture, one of untapped power potential. One of the more impressive BPs @ ACG, exceeding 104EV in every round, then posted in-game, up to 108. Sets up wide & open, angling himself like he's trying to elevate the ball pull-side, but arm-bar steepens the path & prevents him from doing so. Slight mechanical tweaking could result in plus power. Atleast AA runner, 4.07 on jailbreak, & covers both gaps instinctually. BA arm makes LF more likely as of now, but the athleticism will give him a chance to prove himself in CF. Excited G2, tough buy out of Stanford.

LHH catcher with lackluster raw tools but also without any glaring holes to his profile. The closest thing would be swing-and-miss this summer, but adeptly avoided Ks in spring en route to a 1.264 OPS vs elite SoCal competition. Controls the zone well & draws plenty of walks. Limited by raw power output, yet to see him surpass 100EV in-game. Fringy arm; 1.99 avg pop on 10 TM attempts going back to last summer (his best times were all in 2025). Has not instilled confidence in his ability to keep the ball in front. I do think the receiving works, fast hands & steals strikes, but is not a particularly muscular kid, & smaller forearms will likely lead to a regression in receiving once stuff improves. Without any standout traits it's going to be a hard buy, especially considering age, but well worth a follow given spring performance.

Short, stout northeast RHP who's performed at every stage he's faced. 100th% event performance, & 77 K to 13 BB in 53.1 IP this spring, going 6+ innings in over half his starts. Works east-west with low3/4 slot, but low spin limits FB's run. Go-to secondary is SW w feel to command (mvmnt also limited by spin), and occ mixes in CH he struggles to locate. Present stuff has proven more than capable of getting HSers out, but grades-out as well-BA & don't see much room for improvement given mature/small frame & lmtd spin capacity.

Lean, strong frame @ 6'0. Struggled this spring, albeit against elite competition: .224 AVG, 24.7% Ks, 71%contact, but performance took a step forward this summer in small sample. Impressed by the swing decisions, & has produced on FBs, but struggles to make meaningful contact against spin. Swing will take some work, but might be able to project power if he adds counter-rotation/flexion to the load and syncs-up a disconnected forward move. For now, its BA raw power; up to 102EV in-game. Moves well in the outfield, is at least an AVG runner, but combined with BA arm I don't think CF is a realistic end-destination. High G5.

Defense-first NorCal catcher whose muscular build limits mobility. Averaged 1.95 pop & 81.2mph on 4 TM throws this summer. 31% CS as HS Junior. Offensively, he followed-up a poor spring performance where he hit under .300 w minimal power, with an even poorer summer. No glaring struggles with bat-to-ball or swing decisions, but the swing's long & doesn't seem in-control of hanging leg-kick, making it difficult to be on-time. Topped @ 100EV in BP @ ACG, never got there in-game. Solidly 20 runner, not an athletic mover. Age is on his side, but tough demographic to be excited about, even if he'd shown any offensive production. Front-end of G5.

Long arms, wide shoulders, & room to add muscle. Combined w loose/whippy arm, there's plenty of velo to come. In 49 IP as soph, posted a 0.33 ERA, 62 Ks vs NorCal comp. Missed most of this spring with back injury, but dominated this summer, including 3 perfect innings @ ACG. AA extension & high3/4 slot. Creates big shapes w ample spin capacity: hoppy FF that's been a near-automatic chase when thrown above the zone, tight SL, frisbee SW w lmtd usage, & fade-heavy circleCH w plus velo separation (without slowing armspeed). Throws strictly from stretch, but diverse mix & ability to hold velo balance out SP odds. Listed himself as 2-way @ ACG & showed some pop, but swing isn't the prettiest & plays backup SS @ Redwood, RHP profile is a lot more intriguing presently. Worth keeping an eye on.

Skinny frame with room to add muscle @ 6'2, but hurt by age. Plays @ Knights Academy now after beginning HS career in Virginia. Lighter pitch mix thrown from low3/4 slot with AVG extension. The low release might allow FF with deadzone shape to play up if more velo comes, but hitters have feasted on it up to this point. FT is a useful weapon vs R despite low velo. The only OS offering is SW with lmtd feel. Thrown almost exclusively to righties, the pitch has generated tons of swiss in small sample. Big spin capacity in general, but especially on the breaker. Late G5, velo would need to take a step forward this spring to have any real interest.

More velo to come if Lutz can add mass onto tall, skinny frame. Impressive spring campaign, posted a 0.347 K%-BB% in 42.1 innings, albeit vs a weak northeast schedule. Walks became a more concerning aspect of his game this summer. Poor stride direction & open FFS lead to gloveside/high misses. Gets down the mound well & throws from high3/4 slot, utilizing a fleshed-out 4-pitch-mix: FF with some ride but smaller shape overall, firm gyro SL, huge SW w tons of horz, & low-usage CH that effectively kills spin & velo, albeit with lower intent. Loose, whippy arm, syncing up his long limbs/repeatability will be a question to monitor, but a lot to like with this kid.

Projecting velo to come as Hines adds muscle onto thin, long-levered frame. Dominant spring performance: 123 Ks in 59.1 innings, 0.100 BAA. Too many free passes, which became a bigger issue this summer when 10/25 BF @ ACG/ECP reached via BB/HBP. Throws FF & FT but prefers FT, & for good reason: effectively kills IVB, & combined with 5.8 rel height (largely from BA ext, the slot itself is ~3/4) creates genuinely steep VAAs. The key will be locating the pitch down, but hasn't shown ability to do so consistently (shoulders stay closed past FFS, causing too many misses gloveside/high). FB-dominant usage, occ mixes in bad CH & SL w inconsistent mvmnt (flashes armside break at times). No feel for either OS, struggles to repeat ugly arm path. Excited G5, need to see better OS & command.

Canadian RHP with reliever traits, but youth & physical projection on his side. Control struggles define/limit the profile: 21 BB to 68 BF in 2026 Synergy video. OTT deliv w modest extension. 3-pitch-mix @ ACG: ride FF (which gets some pitcher-grader love), FT (which does not), & short SL with AVG spin capacity. Previously showed a slower, more horizontal SW, needed to manipulate slot to attain the shape leading to zero feel. Tough buy out of USC unless he adds muscle this offseason and feel to pitch takes a big step forward.

Physically underdeveloped RHH INF who’s too old to project much growth. Played a reliable SS @ ACG, physicality suggests a transition to 2B eventually but arm, reportedly up to 91mph, will give him a shot on left side. Hand-eye/contact is the carrying trait. Ran a 6% K-rate this spring at Bishop Gorman (NV) with 8 bombs. Hasn’t shown the same pop with wood, but EVs aren’t nothing; up to 103 in-game. Hunts FBs up, amazingly has performed best on FBs above the zone; achieves this with a front-foot-heavy, handsy swing & plenty of batspeed. Very rarely chases OS. I got BA H2F times but supposedly ran a 6.47 60 at PBR ProCase. Hoping he gets taller & stronger by spring, until then it's hard to be head-over-heels about a 155LB 19 year old. Uncommitted currently.

Small yet sturdy frame @ 5'11, 98% event performer. Fills up the zone w 3-pitch-mix. Throws from OTT slot, FF grade will be dependent on ability to maintain big ride. Most intriguing pitch is lifty SL, which has flashed as much as 18in IVB; 58% miss in lmtd Synergy sample. Throws it primarily to righties. CH also has carry, with lmtd separation off FB. Raised his slot even higher @ WWBA Championship, where we saw the biggest carry on his SL, & CH looked like a new (better) pitch: slower & conducive to some ugly swings. Curious as to why he made, then reversed the changes. Tough demographic to be thrilled about, but enough summer performance to warrant some spring attention.

Little will play his 5th HS season @ Phillips Academy after graduating from Dexter Southfield in 2026; 27 BBs in only 11.1 innings across his career thus far (12/2 in 2026). Walks characterize his summer performance as well. Vanilla release traits, employs 2-pitch-mix: true deadzone FB & huge SW w AA spin. Rarely gets chases, but seems more like a case of hitters reading the scouting report than true lack of deception. Would have loved to project muscle onto his lanky frame if he wasn't already so old. The arm isn't nothing, but command would need to take an unrealistic step forward this spring to consider buying this 20 year old HSer (who’s already had TJ) away from UNC.

Well-rounded bat without the summer results to support. Operates out of closed stance. Generally passive vs OS, but impressed by the selective aggression on FBs. 97% Z-Contact this summer, but a mere .278 SLG on those swings. I'm curious how much he's selling out for K-avoidance; regularly surpassed 100EV in BP @ ACG (T105), just never showed up in-game. Extremely impressive spring, where he posted a 1.113 OPS & 12% K-rate against premium competition. Getting some love as LHP, but limited by lackluster stuff. It’s possible given slimmer frame that he’ll add weight & velo by spring, but for now the bat's far more intriguing due to underlying traits/spring stats. Transition to OF is in the cards given arm strength & fringe speed, but playing 1B for Jesuit now.

Physically advanced OF whose upright setup & high hands make it difficult to get the barrel on-plane early, leading to lower launches than you’d like for power-first prof. Saw @ ACG, where the bat produced, including 4 hits over 100EV vs some of the event’s better arms. Strong, fast hands, sprays it to all fields without excessive effort. If adjustments can be made to fix the path, could be +power. Impressive spring campaign: 1.171 OPS, 6 HR, 11 K in 98 PA vs norCal comp. Borderline 20 runner, might be tough to add speed without sacrificing power given his physicality at the plate. Seems to move better underway, but combined with fringe arm, we can hope for COF outcome, with 1B being a worryingly possible end-destination. Late-G2 regardless because I believe in the bat.
